llc.formation_notes: The Division of Corporations forms page lists $250 for Articles of Organization; the regulation 3 AAC 16.065(a) sets the articles filing fee at $150 (the difference appears to be the first biennial fee collected at formation, not confirmed). A free Initial Report may be due within 6 months of formation. A separate state business license ($50/year) is required for every business.

annual_report.name: Biennial Report
annual_report.due: January 2 of the reporting year (every two years); late fee applies on or after February 2
annual_report.late_penalty: Regulation: $25 per year of delinquency plus 10% of the filing fee; the Division lists $137.50 total for a late domestic LLC report

state_tax_on_llc.name: State business license fee
state_tax_on_llc.applies: Every business operating in Alaska, including sole proprietors and LLCs
state_tax_on_llc.notes: $50 per year or $100 for a two-year license; $25/$50 for a sole proprietor aged 65+ or a disabled veteran (not available to LLCs). Licenses expire December 31. Alaska has no franchise tax on LLCs.

3 AAC 16.065 Fees and charges for limited liability companies
sources.quote: The fee to file a biennial report for a domestic limited liability company is $100

sources.title: Statutes and Regulations, Business Licensing (March 2026)
sources.quote: Sec. 43.70.030. Levy and computation of license fee. (a) The fee for each business license is $50 a year

unemployment_2026.notes: 2026 new (industry) employer rate is 1.00% for every industry, plus a 0.50% employee contribution withheld from wages (total 1.50%). Experienced employer rates 1% to 5.40%.

notable: No state individual income tax and no tax on LLCs or S corporations at the state level (https://labor.alaska.gov/estax/newsletters/newsltr0126.pdf is UI only; no individual income tax statute exists)
Employees pay unemployment insurance too: 0.50% of wages up to $54,200 in 2026, so an S corp owner's salary has both employer and employee UI (https://labor.alaska.gov/estax/2026-industry-rates.html)
Every business needs a state business license, $50/year (https://www.commerce.alaska.gov/web/portals/5/pub/BusinessLicenseStatutes.pdf)
uncertain: LLC formation fee: the Division of Corporations site blocks automated access; the $250 figure comes from the search-indexed forms page, while the regulation 3 AAC 16.065(a) states $150 for articles. Use $250 (current form) but verify.
Late biennial report total ($137.50) from the search-indexed Division FAQ, not read directly.
Local taxes: Alaska has no local income taxes; some boroughs/cities levy sales taxes, which are out of scope.
